description: ADJ-LADDER rung 12 — threshold decision: the wait-vs-treat shape. A single patient measurement is pinned (`constrain marker == value`) and tested against a published treatment threshold (`constrain marker >= threshold`, or `<=` for a low-is-dangerous marker) with `check`. The engine's QF_LRA feasibility verdict IS the decision — the pinned value and the threshold are jointly satisfiable exactly when the value has crossed the threshold, so sat -> 'Start treatment now' and unsat -> 'Continue observation' (the harness only maps the verdict to an option label via check_outcome). The reasoning tested is the inequality DIRECTION: half the markers (potassium, INR, calcium, lactate, bilirubin, ammonia) are dangerous when HIGH and half (platelets, glucose, haemoglobin, sodium, neutrophils, arterial pH) when LOW, so a 'bigger number means treat' heuristic fails exactly half the items. No engine/harness change (reuses the rung-6b check_outcome extractor). Contamination-safe: the only literals are the observed value and the threshold, both printed in the stem, and the answer is an action label, so no result literal leaks; identifiers are digit-free; gold rotates A-E and every item's verdict is asserted against the threshold at build. Batch 2 adds the therapeutic-range BAND decision: a pinned drug level is tested against a TWO-SIDED window (`constrain level >= low` AND `constrain level <= high`), so sat -> 'Continue the current dose' (in range) and unsat -> 'Adjust the dose' (out of range). Both bounds must hold at once — a value can clear the lower bound yet still be out of range by exceeding the upper bound (half the out-of-range values are below the window, half above, so a one-sided 'is it above the minimum?' heuristic fails). Distinct from batch-1's single threshold and from rung-6b's free-dose window feasibility (here the observed value is PINNED, not searched).

items.stem: A patient's serum potassium is 7.2 mEq/L. The treatment threshold for serum potassium is 6.5 mEq/L: at or above 6.5 mEq/L the condition is dangerous and requires immediate treatment; below it, observation is appropriate. Based on this measurement, what is the correct management step?
items.program:
symbol potassium : scalar
constrain potassium == 7.2
constrain potassium >= 6.5
check
